data.reasoning: The disagreement is caused by API and parsing errors in two of the models, which prevented them from completing their file reviews. The deepseek model successfully audited all files, including the PKGBUILD, and found a standard, safe Rust cargo package. The source is pinned with a SHA-256 checksum, dependencies are locked, and there are no malicious injection patterns or suspicious network operations in the build scripts.
data.disagreement_analysis: The qwen model encountered HTTP 400 API errors when attempting to review the PKGBUILD and license files, while the openrouter/free model failed to parse its own response for the PKGBUILD. Both resulted in inconclusive verdicts due to tool failures, not security concerns. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found no issues.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review PKGBUILD and license files due to HTTP 400 API errors
openrouter/free model failed to parse PKGBUILD review and only reviewed 1 out of 8 files
learnings: Distinguish between inconclusive verdicts caused by tool/API errors versus those caused by genuinely suspicious code to avoid unnecessary escalations
Implement automatic fallback to a different model if the primary model fails with an API error during the file review phase
